Appearance:
 Shri Mayank Verma - Advocate for appellant appearing th  Conferencing.
Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for respondent No.3.

ORDER This appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 09/04/2021 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Badnawar, District Dhar (M.P.) in MACC No.38/2018, whereby an amount of Rs.4,51,323/- has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 27/03/2018 in favour of the appellant /
claimant / injured with interest @ 6% per annum.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Badnawar, District Dhar (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The case of the appellant is that he has suffered injuries in a Road Traffic Accident occurred on 24/01/2018 at about 04:00 am, when he was riding on his motorcycle with due diligence and was going towards Bhainsola.

When he reached Semalkhedi Choupati nearby house of Thanna Dhakad,
offending vehicle white coloured car bearing registration number MP-14-CB-3344 driven rashly and negligently collided with the motorcycle, NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3403 2 MA-3276-2021 due to which he fall down on the ground thereby suffering grievous injuries and fractures.
He was admitted in District Hospital, Badnawar for treatment.

Incident was reported to the concerned police station and after that he filed claim petition claiming an amount of Rs.9,15,000/- from the respondents jointly and severally in the head of just and proper compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant was 24 years of age on the date of accident and was Mason by profession.

He has suffered fracture of right Thigh and left Femur and Tibia bone, whereby he has suffered disablement up to 55%, whereas learned Claims Tribunal has assessed the disability to the extent of 22% only, which is on lower side.

He further submits that income of the appellant was to be assessed on guess work as he could not adduce any cogent evidence in this regard, therefore, as per the circular issued by the Labour Department of State of Gattulal vs Ramesh Solanki on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/192533305/
1

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Gattulal vs Ramesh Solanki
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Madhya Pradesh under the Minimum Wages Act income should have been taken as Rs.7,125/- per month, which has been taken only as Rs.6,000/- per month by the learned Claims Tribunal, which is again on lower side.

As per para 59.4 of the judgment by the Apex Court in the case of National Ins. Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 , 40% was to be added in the head of Future Prospects, which has not been given.

entities.text: National Ins. Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
He further submits that in the heads of Pain and Suffering; Attendant; Conveyance; and Special Diet, the amount awarded is on lower side,
therefore, prays for enhancement of the amount in the aforesaid heads thereby enhancing the total award amount.
On these submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3403 3 MA-3276-2021 4 .

Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3 / Insurance Company opposes the prayer on the ground that all the relevant evidence adduced by the parties have been considered and no enhancement is required.
The appeal has no merit, hence liable to be dismissed.

5. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.

It is well settled that where income of the injured is not fixed or proved by any documentary evidence, then income should be taken as per the slab fixed under the Minimum Wages Act vide circular issued by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, therefore, income of the appellant / injured should have been taken as Rs.7,125/- in place of Rs.6,000/- by considering him as unskilled labour.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 7. On the basis of the evidence adduced, this Court is of the view that the learned Claims Tribunal has rightly assessed the disability to the extent of 22%, requires no interferenc 8.

Looking to the age 24 years of the appellant, in the light of the para 59.4 of the judgment by the Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) , an addition of 40% should be in the head of Future Prospects.

9. The amount awarded in the heads of Pain and Suffering; Attendant; and Conveyance, also appears on lower side, therefore, in these heads the amount of compensation is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-; Rs.10,000/-; and Rs.10,000/- respectively.

10. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3403 4 MA-3276-2021 Income per month Rs.7,125.00 + Rs.2,850.00 (40% Future Prospects) = Permanent Rs.9,975.00 per month = Rs.2,194.50 Disability: (22% Permanent Disability) x 12 = Rs.26,334.00 x 18 (Multiplier) = Rs.4,74,012.00
Medical Rs.1,13,203.00

Expenses:
Pain & Rs.20,000.00

Suffering:

2 Attendant: Rs.10,000.00
Conveyance: Rs.10,000.00
Special Diet: Rs.5,000.00 Loss of Rs.42,750.00

Income:
 Total: Rs.6,74,965.00

MACT  Rs.4,51,323.00  Awarded:
 Enhanced Rs.2,23,642.00 (Round Off  Amount: to Rs.2,24,000.00
Thus, the amount is enhanced and appellant / claimant is entitled to an additional amount of Rs.2,24,000/- over and above the amount, which has been awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
11. Resultantly, the appeal filed by the appellant / claimant is allowed to the extent as indicated hereinabove.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
